rationales: Carbon-14 is mainly used for dating and tracing, not internal cancer treatment.
Phosphorus-32 can be used as an internal radiation treatment for certain cancers.
Cobalt-60 is chiefly used as an external radiation source for cancer treatment.
Strontium-90 is not the isotope used for this internal cancer treatment.
Compounds are chemically combined and cannot be separated by physical means.
Radicals are groups of atoms, not mixtures separable by physical methods.
Elements cannot be broken down into simpler substances by physical means.
Mixtures can be separated into their components by physical means.
A triple covalent bond shares three pairs, or six electrons.
Four electrons make two shared pairs, as in a double bond.
Three electrons do not make a complete triple-bonded set of shared pairs.
Eight electrons are not involved in a single triple covalent bond.
A metal and a nonmetal typically form an ionic bond by electron transfer.
An ionic bond is expected because electrons transfer from the metal to the nonmetal.
A coordinate covalent bond involves a shared pair donated by one atom, not the usual metal–nonmetal bonding.
A metallic bond occurs between metal atoms.
% m/v expresses grams of solute per 100 cm³ of solution.
% m/m expresses grams of solute per 100 grams of solution.
% v/v expresses cm³ of solute per 100 cm³ of solution.
% v/m expresses cm³ of solute per 100 grams of solution.
Water formation is not an acid–base reaction.
Hydrogen is oxidized and oxygen is reduced, so water formation is a redox reaction.
Water is formed by combination, not by decomposition.
No acid and base are neutralizing each other to form water here.
Some metals, such as sodium, form unipositive ions, but not all metal ions do.
Some metals, such as calcium, form dipositive ions, but not all metal ions do.
Some metals, such as aluminium, form tripositive ions, but not all metal ions do.
Metals can form unipositive, dipositive, or tripositive ions.
Sodium chloride is soluble in water.
Potassium chloride is soluble in water.
Calcium chloride is soluble in water.
Benzene, C₆H₆, is not soluble in water.
Na is the symbol for sodium.
Ca is the symbol for calcium.
Ag is the symbol for silver.
Si is the symbol for silicon.
Canal rays consist of positively charged particles.
Canal rays are not negatively charged.
Canal rays carry charge, so they are not neutral.
Canal rays carry a positive, not partial negative, charge.
Periods are the horizontal rows of the modern periodic table.
Groups are the vertical columns of the modern periodic table.
Noble gases occupy a group; they are not the name for all vertical columns.
Transition elements occupy part of the table and are not the name for vertical columns.
Transfer of electrons between atoms forms an ionic bond.
A covalent bond forms by sharing electrons rather than transferring them.
Metallic bonding involves delocalized electrons among metal atoms.
A coordinate covalent bond forms when one atom donates a shared pair.
Hydrogen has the lowest molecular mass among these gases and diffuses fastest.
Helium is heavier than hydrogen, so it diffuses more slowly.
Fluorine molecules are much heavier than hydrogen molecules and diffuse more slowly.
Chlorine molecules are much heavier than hydrogen molecules and diffuse more slowly.
A 2 M solution is the most concentrated option and has the least water per amount of solution.
A 1 M solution is more concentrated than the lower-molarity choices.
A 0.5 M solution is more concentrated than the 0.25 M solution.
A 0.25 M solution is the most dilute option and therefore contains the most water for the same solution volume.
Liquids are generally denser than gases by more than 100 times.
Liquids are approximately 1000 times denser than gases in the usual textbook comparison.
A factor of 10000 is too large for the usual comparison between liquids and gases.
A factor of 100000 is too large for the usual comparison between liquids and gases.
